key_insight: Drive My Way (DMW) enables a single vision-language-action model to adapt driving behavior to individual drivers by conditioning actions on natural‑language preferences and inferred long‑term habits, providing personalized, interpretable control over autonomous driving.
problem_solved: Existing end-to-end driving systems are optimized for generic objectives or fixed modes and cannot flexibly adapt to individual driver preferences or accept natural‑language intent, limiting personalization and interpretability.
method: Train a multimodal vision–language–action (VLA) model that maps visual input and vehicle state plus a natural‑language preference token to driving actions.

Align the VLA model to individual preferences using preference-conditioned learning (combining demonstrations, preference signals or comparisons, and behavior cloning / reward modeling) so long‑term habits and short‑term intents are respected.
Enable interpretable, real‑time adaptation by exposing natural‑language controls and a preference embedding that modulates planning/action outputs.
impact: Makes autonomous driving systems more human‑centric by allowing per‑driver personalization and natural‑language control, improving acceptability, comfort, and transparency for deployment and research in adaptive decision-making.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: camera + state + language preference → VLA model → personalized control outputs (steer/accel/brake).
Before vs After comparison: generic policy vs DMW personalized trajectories in a corner case (e.g., merging/over‑taking).
Preference embedding illustration: how long‑term habits and short‑term intent combine to produce different action distributions.
UI mockup: driver issuing natural‑language preference (e.g., “drive conservatively” or “merge assertively”) and resulting behavior preview.
paper_title: Drive My Way: Preference Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model for Personalized Driving
paper_authors: Zehao Wang, Huaide Jiang, Shuaiwu Dong, Yuping Wang, Hang Qiu
